analysis.title: The Gold Standard: Market Review – October 30
key_insights: The S&P 500 fell 0.6% in the week to Oct 30 to 7,580 and the VIX was flat at about 19.5. The Nasdaq Composite fell 2.0% and S&P information technology fell 1.8%.
The 10Y Treasury yield fell 7bps to 4.93%. The real yield fell 6bps to 2.59% and 10Y inflation expectations fell 1bp to 2.34%. The 2s10s curve narrowed 2bps to 0.34%.
The DXY dollar index rose 0.2% to 102.0. The Brazilian real weakened 1.3% and the Indian rupee 1.2% against the dollar.
Gold fell 3.0% on the week to $3,875/oz, the low of its 52-week range ($3,875 to $5,417). It is down 10.3% YTD and 6.8% over one month.
Silver fell 8.9% to $49.10/oz, platinum fell 7.6% and palladium fell 6.5%. Silver is down 31.5% YTD.
Physical gold ETFs recorded outflows of 203koz on the week, with holdings at 101.1moz. Physical silver ETFs recorded inflows of 3moz, with holdings at 809moz.
CFTC net long gold positions fell 12k to 180k contracts and net long silver was flat to 17k contracts. Both figures are as of Oct 27.
Gold equities fell 3.9% (GDX $77.09) and GDXJ fell 4.4%. Gold equity ETFs saw inflows of $25m and silver equity ETFs saw inflows of $228m.

The top weekly gold equity movers relative to the index were Greatland Resources (+13.5%), FireFly Metals (+10.6%) and Westgold Resources (+10.4%). The worst were DPM Metals (-13.3%), Kinross Gold (-9.9%) and G Mining (-9.6%).
Energy is strong: WTI rose 0.8% to $104.12/bbl and Brent rose 1.5% to $113.43. WTI is up 81.3% YTD and diesel is $6.19/gal. S&P energy is up 56.6% YTD.
Copper fell 0.4% to $6.48/lb and Bitcoin fell 4.5% to $76.7k, down 12.4% quarter to date.
Gold's 3-month correlation with the 10Y TIPS yield is -0.13 and with the dollar index is -0.38. The 1-year correlations are -0.36 and -0.40.
The gold to silver ratio is 79x against a 10-year average of 81x. The gold to copper ratio is 603x against a 10-year average of 544x and the gold to oil ratio is 37x against 32x.
Short interest increased at Perpetua Resources and decreased at Fortuna Mining and SSR Mining. GDX short interest is 9.7% of float and GLD is 4.9%. Short interest is as of Oct 15.
S&P telecom services fell 8.5% on the week, the largest sector decline. Brazil's Bovespa fell 18.1%.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The yield fell 7bps on the week, driven mostly by a 6bps drop in real yields.
The real yield fell 6bps and gold fell 3.0% over the same week.
Market inflation expectations fell 1bp on the week.
The curve narrowed 2bps on the week.
A chart caption shows US CPI at 3.7% YoY, against Eurozone 3.8%, China 0.9% and Japan 2.1%.
A chart caption shows PPI at 6.3% YoY and import prices at 8.1% YoY.
A chart caption shows CPI up 0.6% MoM, PPI up 1.3% and import prices flat.
The dollar index rose 0.2% on the week and sits near the top of its 52-week range (96.2 to 102.6).
The index table shows HY OAS down 14bps on the week. The credit chart caption shows HY at 368bps and IG at 126bps, which conflicts with the 323bps and 87bps in the table.

crypto_views: Bitcoin fell 4.5% on the week to $76.7k, down 8.2% over one month, up 18.6% over three months and down 28.6% over one year.
risk_factors: Gold is at the bottom of its 52-week range and fell 3.0% on the week despite lower real yields, so the usual inverse link to real yields did not hold this week.
A stronger dollar (DXY +0.2% to 102.0) and a broad precious metals selloff (silver -8.9%, platinum -7.6%, palladium -6.5%) point to pressure on the complex.
WTI at $104.12 and Brent at $113.43 sit near the top of their 52-week ranges, and diesel is up 78.3% YTD.
Gold miners have fallen about 12% over one month, and junior and exploration names have fallen more, with equal-weighted declines of about 18% to 22% over the month.
Brazil's Bovespa fell 18.1% on the week and the Brazilian real weakened 1.3%.

vol_and_positioning: The VIX was flat at 19.4 to 19.5. The CBOE Gold ETF Volatility Index (GVZ) rose 1.8% to 26.2.
CFTC net long gold fell 11.9k to 179.9k contracts, down 30.3k over one month and down 39.6k year to date. Net long silver is 17k contracts.
Other CFTC net positions: copper 48k (-9k), S&P 500 15k (+2k), USD -65k (+8k), CAD -1000k (-138k), 2-year Treasury -134k (+8k), 10-year Treasury -971k (-21k).
GDX short interest is 9.7% of float (up 0.9%) and GDXJ is 6.3%. SLV is 5.5% and GLD is 4.9%, up 2.1% from the last period.
Highest short interest as a share of float among gold equities: Hycroft Mining 23.7%, McEwen 22.1%, Perpetua 16.9%, Silvercorp 15.6% and I-80 Gold 15.4%.
Weekly GDX and GDXJ flows were +$25m, quarter-to-date flows are +$0m and YTD flows are -$208m. Silver equity ETF (SIL and SILJ) flows were +$228m.
